detail.title: Computational Creativity and Autonomous Problem Formulation
detail.summary: Autonomous problem formulation relies on decomposing tasks into formulation, representation, manipulation, and evaluation components, while cognitive effort—mediated by active inference and drift-diffusion mechanisms—governs the transition between habitual behaviors and optimal policies.
detail.reason: Incorporating active inference mechanisms into the existing problem-solving framework enhances the structural understanding of how agents identify and prioritize novel problems.
